solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Do avoid that hot sauce (3,3,7)

blocks.note: to cut someone is to avoid or ignore them
the definite article, as in 'that one' = 'the one'

annotation.surface: Advice to someone about to eat: steer clear of the fiery sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as a kitchen instruction, 'Do' looks like the start of a command; it is the definition, meaning 'be good enough', as in 'that will do'.
annotation.definitionFit: To cut the mustard is to be good enough, which is what something does when it will do.

entries.clue: French philosopher quietly barred from college grounds (5)

indicatorNotes.barred from: the P is shut out of the word, so it leaves

blocks.note: the grounds of a college or university
p = piano, quietly in music; it is removed

annotation.surface: A French thinker being kept off a university site.
annotation.walkthrough: Albert Camus, the writer of The Outsider, is the philosopher; the surface's banning order is literally what happens to the P.
annotation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was a French philosopher and novelist associated with absurdism.

entries.clue: Puzzling pieces of square brown mass (7)

blocks.note: a gram is a unit of mass

annotation.surface: Some baffling bits of a square that is brown and heavy.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition runs longer than it looks: 'Puzzling pieces of square' is the whole of it, since a tangram is a square cut into seven pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A tangram is a Chinese puzzle of seven pieces cut from a square and rearranged into shapes.

entries.clue: Giddy bachelor showered, taking maiden’s place in seraglio (11)

indicatorNotes.taking maiden’s place in: B moves into the spot where M stood in HAREM

blocks.note: m = maiden, a cricket over with no runs; it is swapped out
b = bachelor; it takes M's place, making HAREB

annotation.surface: A dizzy single man takes a shower and then stands in for a woman in a harem.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored, hence M; the one-letter swap happens before the weather word is added.
annotation.definitionFit: Harebrained means rash or flighty, much like giddy in its sense of frivolous.

entries.clue: Reflecting less concern (6)

blocks.note: more matt, the comparative of matt, a surface that shines less
a concern here is a business or affair, the noun

annotation.surface: Someone thinking about things less and so caring less.
annotation.walkthrough: The trick is reading MATTER as matt + -er: a matt finish reflects less light than a glossy one. 'Reflecting' pretends to mean thinking.
annotation.definitionFit: Two plain senses: the comparative of matt, a dull finish that throws back less light, and the noun for an affair, as in 'a matter for the police'.

entries.clue: Arctic hunter broadcast cry of distress around north (5,3)

indicatorNotes.around: Something placed around another encloses it, so SOW wraps itself about the N.

blocks.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it by scattering
n = north, placed inside SOW to make SNOW
a yowl is a loud wail

annotation.surface: A radio message about a hunter in the far north sending a distress call.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' and 'cry of distress' together suggest an SOS on the radio; broadcast is the farmer's word, sowing seed by hand.
annotation.definitionFit: The snowy owl is a large white owl that hunts on the Arctic tundra.

entries.clue: One speed if short of power (3)

indicatorNotes.short of: To be short of something is to lack it, so the speed word goes without its P.

annotation.surface: A single gear on a vehicle that is underpowered.
annotation.walkthrough: An ace is the one in a pack of cards, which is why 'One' can define it.
annotation.definitionFit: The ace is the card valued at one, and on dice the one-spot face.

entries.clue: Peter out first on deck, totally calm abandoning ship (7)

indicatorNotes.abandoning: To abandon ship is to leave it, so the SS departs from the calm word.

annotation.surface: A becalmed sailing scene where Peter comes up on deck first and then leaves the ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a sailor's name; with 'out' it is the verb meaning to fade away.
annotation.definitionFit: To peter out is to diminish gradually to nothing, which is what dwindling does.

entries.clue: American blues fan daughter converted to Cream (8)

indicatorNotes.converted: the letters are changed into a new form

annotation.surface: An American blues lover whose daughter has come round to the rock band Cream.
annotation.walkthrough: In US politics blue is the Democrats' colour, so a blues fan is a Democrat supporter, not a music lover; Cream was a 1960s blues-rock band.
annotation.definitionFit: Blue states vote Democratic, so an American who backs the blues is a Democrat.

entries.clue: Live in effectively brand-new tower (7)

indicatorNotes.in: One word goes in another, the plain sense of placing something inside.

blocks.note: in mint condition = as good as new
to be is to live: 'we are' = 'we live'

annotation.surface: Moving into a tower block that has only just been built.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Live in' reads as one phrase about residence; 'in' is really the container instruction, and 'effectively brand-new' is a single idea, as good as new.
annotation.definitionFit: Tower is the general word; a minaret is one particular kind, the slender tower beside a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

entries.clue: Earlier group taken through Yosemite now back (3-4)

indicatorNotes.group taken through: a run of letters is lifted from across the words
indicatorNotes.back: the run reads right to left

blocks.note: yosEMITE NOw contains the letters, which are then read backwards

annotation.surface: An old party of hikers passing through Yosemite and now returning.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words, so the national park is only a letter carrier here.
annotation.definitionFit: One-time means former, as in 'a one-time champion', i.e. earlier.

entries.clue: Rose’s bed maybe quiet and springy (9)

annotation.surface: A woman named Rose has a soft, bouncy, peaceful bed.
annotation.walkthrough: Rose looks like a person's name with a mattress; it is the flower, and her bed is a garden bed.
annotation.definitionFit: A shrubbery is an area planted with shrubs, which may be where roses grow.

entries.clue: Valued bijou scratched in odd places, reproduction you hear (5)

indicatorNotes.scratched in odd places: letters 1, 3, 5... are struck out, keeping the even ones

annotation.surface: A precious little trinket that has been scratched in places.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scratched' deletes rather than marks, and 'odd places' says which letters go.
annotation.definitionFit: Audio is recorded or transmitted sound, a reproduction that you listen to.

entries.clue: Spooner’s bred ’ackneys etc for the military (5,6)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: farmed = bred; it hands its F over
hackneys and the like are horses, with the H dropped as the apostrophe shows; it takes the F

annotation.surface: Horses bred for use by the army, in a Cockney-flavoured spelling.
annotation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'ackneys matters: FARMED 'ORSES has only the F to swap, giving ARMED FORCES. A hackney is a breed of horse.
annotation.definitionFit: The armed forces are a country's military services taken together.

entries.clue: Gong with two sides, neither having echo (3-3)

indicatorNotes.neither having: If neither of the two has something, it is missing from both, so each copy goes without the E.

blocks.note: a side is a team; two of them
Echo is E in the radio alphabet; removed from each TEAM

annotation.surface: A gong that can be struck on both faces yet gives back no echo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Two sides' sounds like the faces of the gong; it means two teams, each shedding its E.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the tam-tam is the orchestra's large flat bronze gong, named after its sound.

entries.clue: Ill-judged time to show more of the real you? (8)

blocks.clueFragment: to show more of the real you?
blocks.note: to act less, putting on less of a performance

annotation.surface: Asking whether it is a bad moment to reveal your true self.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'show more of the real you' is a playful way of saying ACT LESS.
annotation.definitionFit: A tactless remark is ill-judged, lacking sensitivity.

entries.clue: Curse, stuffing one’s weight in bikini? (8)

indicatorNotes.stuffing: Stuffing something fills its inside, so the curse word is filled with the other letters.

annotation.surface: Cursing at squeezing into a bikini.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark says a bikini is only an example of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: the bikini is a single instance of the whole category.

entries.clue: Italian greeting chief heard order in Chinese (4,4)

indicatorNotes.heard: what we want is how the words sound

annotation.surface: A leading Italian giving a command in a Chinese language.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as a command; it is a meal ordered in a Chinese restaurant.
annotation.definitionFit: Chow mein is a dish of fried noodles often ordered at a Chinese takeaway.

entries.clue: Light speed and Mach one confused Native American (8)

indicatorNotes.confused: Something confused is jumbled and out of order, so these letters are rearranged.

blocks.note: c is the physicists' symbol for the speed of light

annotation.surface: Someone muddled by light speed versus the speed of sound.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Light speed and Mach one' reads as physics; the first contributes just C, the second its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The Comanche are a Native American people of the southern Great Plains.

entries.clue: Drink from craft baby bottles (7)

indicatorNotes.bottles: To bottle something is to hold it inside a container, so one word holds the other.

annotation.surface: Feeding a baby from hand-crafted bottles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' looks like a noun about feeding a baby; it is the verb, MINI bottling ART.
annotation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

entries.clue: Instructed party returned small batch of shares (3,3)

indicatorNotes.returned: TOLD DO comes back reading right to left

annotation.surface: A group of people who were given orders came back with a few shares.
annotation.walkthrough: TOLD DO read backwards is ODD LOT. On a stock exchange an odd lot is a holding smaller than the usual trading unit.
annotation.definitionFit: An odd lot is a quantity of shares less than the standard round lot.

entries.clue: Gap between seats Romeo spread with girl’s clothing (7)

annotation.surface: A lover sprawling across the aisle with his girlfriend's clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: Romeo wants to be the R of the radio alphabet; here all five letters are fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Legroom is the space in front of a seat, such as the gap to the next row.

entries.clue: Commercial imperative the very thing academic is superior to (6)

indicatorNotes.is superior to: in a down answer PROF sits above IT

blocks.note: 'it' as in 'that's it', exactly what's wanted

annotation.surface: Business needs versus the ideal, which the scholar claims to stand above.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Superior' sounds snobbish; in a down clue it just means placed above.
annotation.definitionFit: Profit is what every commercial business must make.

entries.clue: Horribly bright — you are to wear hat (5)

indicatorNotes.to wear: UR goes inside LID as a head goes inside a hat

blocks.note: lid is slang for a hat

annotation.surface: Being told to put on a hat that is garishly coloured.
annotation.walkthrough: 'You are' becomes text-speak, and the surface's order to put on a hat is the literal instruction: the hat goes round the pair.
annotation.definitionFit: Lurid means unpleasantly vivid in colour.

entries.clue: Belligerent type of friendly against Germany (9)

annotation.surface: An aggressive player in a friendly football match against Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Friendly' reads as a noun, a non-competitive match; it is the adjective WARM.
annotation.definitionFit: A warmonger is someone eager for war, a belligerent person.

entries.clue: Outside the church, troops brought round for the king (5)

indicatorNotes.brought round: Bringing something round turns it to face the other way, so the letters are read backwards.

annotation.surface: Soldiers gathering outside a church for the monarch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like a container instruction; 'outside the church' means not ordained, the laity. OR, other ranks, is the army's term for soldiers who are not officers.
annotation.definitionFit: Royal means belonging to or fit for a king.

entries.clue: Hollow stick, one where it’s icy? (3,4)

annotation.definition: Hollow stick, one where it’s icy?

indicatorNotes.Hollow: the word is emptied, leaving only its outside

annotation.surface: Asking about a hollow stick used on ice.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: read straight, it describes a light tubular stick used on snow and ice.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: ski poles are hollow metal sticks, one in each hand, used on icy slopes, so the whole clue reads as a straight description.

entries.clue: Two blood types primarily form clot (3)

indicatorNotes.primarily: just the first letter of form

annotation.surface: Two blood groups that start a clot forming.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is medical, where a clot is blood; in British slang a clot is a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: Clot is British slang for a clumsy fool, a plain synonym once the medical sense is set aside.

entries.clue: Blue-collar employer snubbed brave politician (7)

indicatorNotes.snubbed: cut short, as a snub nose is short

blocks.note: to brave something is to face it
a Tory is a British Conservative

annotation.surface: A factory owner who cold-shoulders a courageous MP.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snubbed' reads as a social slight; here it docks the end of FACE. 'Brave' is the verb, not the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A factory employs manual, blue-collar workers.

entries.clue: During shivery semifinal it’s almost zero (13)

indicatorNotes.shivery: Something shivery trembles and shakes, and shaken letters fall into a new order.

blocks.note: in = during, as in 'in the war'

annotation.surface: A nervous semifinalist whose chances are next to nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining wordplay to definition; IT belongs to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Infinitesimal means vanishingly small, all but zero.
